title: Small Hands at Speed
hook: The lane is straight. The wheel wants a yank.
scene: Wind, afternoon, I-90 east still in the valley. Three lanes this way. The Ledger sits in the center. A gust leans the box a hand's width toward the skip-dash. The quiet-street habit is a big correction. At this speed a yank is yaw, and yaw is the thing that draws. The paint is still yours if the hands stay small.
decision: The gust moved you. How do you put the box back?

options.text: Yank the wheel back to center the way you would on a side street
options.result: The box steps the other way. Yaw at highway speed. The right tires kiss the rumble. You taught the wind it could have you.

options.text: Ease a few degrees, hold, let the box settle in the lane
options.result: The wheel moves a little. The box comes back without a sway. The skip-dash stays a line, not a fight. Small hands kept the schedule quiet.

options.text: Stand on the brake first so the correction happens at a lower number
options.result: You dump speed in the center lane. The stack behind you lights up. You spent their brakes to fix a lean a quiet wheel would have eaten.

options.text: Steer onto the left rumble so you have a bigger target to recover from
options.result: You put the right rear tires on the rumble on purpose. The box hops. Recovery from a rumble at this speed is the crash the gust was not.

debrief: At highway speed, steer gently. A yank is yaw. Keep the wheel small enough that the box never sways.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part two
source.teaching_target: Excessive steering at highway speed risks loss of control; keep corrections small.
